newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Indian prime minister arrives in Mauritius.
newsitem.headline: Indian prime minister arrives in Mauritius.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda arrived in Mauritius on Tuesday for a two-day visit to strengthen already close ties with the Indian Ocean island.
Deve Gowda will be present on Wednesday at the signing of a bilateral credit agreement for the development of technology in Mauritius.
"My visit to Mauritius...is testimony to the special regard for each other. I am convinced our two countries can strengthen our mutually beneficial and rewarding partnership" he said.
Mauritius shares close ties with India, which was its third largest source of imports valued at 2.9 billion rupees ($145 million) in 1995 out of a total of 34.4 billion rupees.
India also accounts for about 90 percent of business in the offshore sector of Mauritius. A majority of the island's 1.1 million people are of Hindu origin.
